<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 22"
    pfs=""
>
[Spiral Athame](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1817)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Blood Lords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #186: Ghost King's Rage](/Sources.aspx?ID=189) pg. 79

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The pommel of this +4 [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [disruptive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=294) [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) [high-grade silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) [dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3) is a black glass orb that contains a tiny blue comet that spirals through the orb's interior. Strikes with the dagger deal an additional 1d8 positive damage to worshippers of [Urgathoa](/Deities.aspx?ID=19) and to anyone who has ever created or [summoned](/Traits.aspx?ID=154) an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature.

 While the dagger is in your possession, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) checks and to [Midwifery Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) checks. If you're a worshipper of [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14), you gain [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) with a range of 60 feet while holding the dagger. If you're undead or a worshipper of Urgathoa, you're [stupefied 4](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) while holding the dagger.

 Despite its utility in combat, the _Spiral Athame_ is intended as a ritual implement, meant to bless newborns and protect them from the predations of undead. If you use the _Spiral Athame_ to cut the umbilical cord of a newly born creature, that creature gains resistance to negative damage equal to their level (minimum 1) and gains a +2 status bonus to saving throws against [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects and [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117). These bonuses are permanent. Additionally, that creature can never become an undead creature.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, interact ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117))    **Effect** You point the _Spiral Athame_ at a corpse within 30 feet, shielding it from corruption. The _Spiral Athame_ casts 5th-level [_gentle repose_](/Spells.aspx?ID=131) on the corpse.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, interact ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117))    **Effect** You point the _Spiral Athame_ to the sky and pray, warding creatures against undead. This has the effect of 3rd-level [_circle of protection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=38), except it wards against undead creatures rather than creatures of a specified alignment, and the emanation is centered on the _Spiral Athame_.

**Destruction** If an undead creature uses the _Spiral Athame_ to slay a [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) usher while within the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15), the _Spiral Athame's_ pommel shatters and the _Spiral Athame_ becomes a mundane, high-grade silver dagger with no special abilities.

</column>

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 76 **Price** 2,500 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- _Spiral chimes_ are a set of small metal bells decorated with spiraling designs that hang on thin wires from a carved statue of a storm cloud or air elemental. Each bell in the spiral chimes rings at a different tone, and when caught in the turbulent winds of a storm, the bells combine to create deep, full songs. A set of spiral chimes is a planar key for [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222) and similar magic. When the chimes are used this way, you're more likely to arrive where you intend to be, appearing 1d6×25 miles from your intended destination instead of 1d10×25 miles away. **Activate—Forecast Chime** 10 minutes ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [prediction](/Traits.aspx?ID=132)) **Effect** You let the _spiral chimes_ play in the wind, interpreting the music to predict the weather at your location for the next 24 hours. You receive advanced warning of the temperature, humidity, storms, natural disasters (such as tornadoes, floods, or volcanic eruptions), and other weather conditions that naturally arise. The information you gain through the _spiral chimes_ doesn't take magical occurrences that might change the weather into account. **Activate—Revealing Chime** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You ring the chimes, blanketing everything in a 30-foot burst within 120 feet in visible, reverberating sound. This can negate invisibility, making creatures [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) instead of [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26). The duration and other effects depend on the result of each creature's attempt at a DC 30 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target's invisibility is negated for 2 rounds.
**Failure** The target is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 minute, and its invisibility is negated for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The target is deafened for 10 minutes, and its invisibility is negated for 10 minutes.

This elegant black, gold-tipped _+1 striking [fighting fan](/Weapons.aspx?ID=284)_  is adorned with images of three golden leaves and a red rope tassel. If a creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points by a spirit fan, the golden leaves on the fan light up, providing illumination equal to that of a torch for 1 minute. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** The _spirit fan's_ leaves are illuminated; **Effect** You sweep the _spirit fan_ in the direction of a single target you can see within 30 feet, releasing the life energy in the form of a streak of golden light. The spirit fan goes dark. If the target is a living creature, the energy restores 3d8+8 Hit Points. If the target is undead, it takes 2d8+8 positive damage (DC 23 basic Fortitude save).

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 90 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This complicated snare is affixed with various crystals and Stasian coils attached to strange electrical relays, working on the same principles as etheric [spirit singers](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1138). When an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creature enters its square, the device lets loose an ectoplasmic web that lashes around the creature's spectral form. The creature must succeed a DC 26 Reflex saving throw or become [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature becomes immobilized for 1 minute. In either case, the incorporeal creature can attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 26).

May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts **Source** [Season of Ghosts (Hardcover)](/Sources.aspx?ID=294) pg. 298 **Price** 5 gp **Bulk** L --- A _spirit trap_ consists of a net dipped in water that has been steeped with sacred herbs to better combat phantoms. This snare’s components function as a net when not set up. You set this snare up in a 10-foot-by-10-foot area. The first creature with the [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) trait that steps into the area must attempt a DC 16 Fortitude save. [Additional rules for snares appear here](/Rules.aspx?ID=3315). **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature is immobilized until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 16).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Spirit-Singer](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1138)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 83

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Etheric spirit-singers create an eerie spectral sound based on the presence of spiritual essence and other ethereal energies. All spirit-singers can be used as musical instruments by manipulating the sensitivity to ethereal energies. However, they have an even greater benefit in areas heavy with spiritual essence. When played in the presence of a significant spiritual disturbance, such as a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) or an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), a spirit-singer grants you a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. While playing a spirit-singer, you also gain a +1 item bonus to checks to detect a haunt or incorporeal undead, and you can roll a check to notice a haunt even if you aren't actively [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) for it, due to the distortions of the spirit-singer's music. A haunt or incorporeal undead that is intelligent enough to notice the effects it is having on the spirit-singer's music and that can't otherwise communicate with the living might choose to use the spirit-singer to do so if it wishes. For instance, it could try to guide the spirit-singer player towards a location by creating distortions in that direction or, if it understands language, it could try to answer questions by creating one distortion for yes and two distortions for no. Unless stated otherwise in its usage entry, a spirit-singer functions like a heavy [musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37); rather than carrying it, the musician places the spirit-singer in a particular position and uses both hands to play.

Etheric spirit-singers create an eerie spectral sound based on the presence of spiritual essence and other ethereal energies. All spirit-singers can be used as musical instruments by manipulating the sensitivity to ethereal energies. However, they have an even greater benefit in areas heavy with spiritual essence. When played in the presence of a significant spiritual disturbance, such as a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) or an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160), a spirit-singer grants you a +1 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. While playing a spirit-singer, you also gain a +1 item bonus to checks to detect a haunt or incorporeal undead, and you can roll a check to notice a haunt even if you aren't actively [Searching](/Actions.aspx?ID=519) for it, due to the distortions of the spirit-singer's music. A haunt or incorporeal undead that is intelligent enough to notice the effects it is having on the spirit-singer's music and that can't otherwise communicate with the living might choose to use the spirit-singer to do so if it wishes. For instance, it could try to guide the spirit-singer player towards a location by creating distortions in that direction or, if it understands language, it could try to answer questions by creating one distortion for yes and two distortions for no. Unless stated otherwise in its usage entry, a spirit-singer functions like a heavy [musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37); rather than carrying it, the musician places the spirit-singer in a particular position and uses both hands to play.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=425)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840) [crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=425)_ has an array of crystalline lenses and silver fittings along the stock and feels strangely light.

**Activate—Ethereal Vision** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You aim through the crossbow's crystalline lenses, gaining imprecise vision onto the [Ethereal Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=34) with a range of 60 feet in addition to your normal senses until the end of your turn. You can sense through objects in the Universe this way, and the sense is precise for detecting creatures. Because this sense detects spiritual energy, a creature that's immune to spirit can't be detected in this way.

**Activate—Ethereal Shot** <actions string="Single Action" /> ;    **Requirements** Ethereal Vision is active; **Effect** You Strike with the _spiritsight crossbow_. This shot travels through the Ethereal Plane, allowing it to pass through and ignore cover from physical objects within the range of your Ethereal Vision.

[Spiritsight Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1526)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 81, [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 154

**Price** 225 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The opal set in this intricately carved ivory ring eventually becomes translucent and tickles your finger whenever an [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creature is nearby. When in the presence of a nearby incorporeal creature, even if it's within a solid object, you eventually detect the creature, though you might not do so instantly, and you can't pinpoint the location. This acts as a [vague sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413), similar to humans' sense of smell. An incorporeal creature trying to hide its presence from this sense attempts a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to hide from your vague sense, as normal for attempting to foil [special senses](/Rules.aspx?ID=414). You gain a +2 item bonus when using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) incorporeal creatures within 30 feet of you.

</column>

</row>

</column>

---

A _spiritual warhorn_ is a trumpet made of horn, leather, and metal. When you play a single, long note from the warhorn, it calls forth a number of Medium spiritual manifestations of warriors to aid you, according to the horn's type. Each warrior appears in an open square adjacent to an enemy within 60 feet of you, makes a Strike for 2d6 force damage (with an attack bonus determined by the warhorn's type), and then disappears. The warriors can flank with one another and with you and your allies.

Once the magic is used, the warhorn remains as a non-magical [musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37).

---

A _spiritual warhorn_ is a trumpet made of horn, leather, and metal. When you play a single, long note from the warhorn, it calls forth a number of Medium spiritual manifestations of warriors to aid you, according to the horn's type. Each warrior appears in an open square adjacent to an enemy within 60 feet of you, makes a Strike for 2d6 force damage (with an attack bonus determined by the warhorn's type), and then disappears. The warriors can flank with one another and with you and your allies.

Once the magic is used, the warhorn remains as a non-magical [musical instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37).

This portable nozzle-and-trigger assembly based on spider spinnerets can extrude and weave alchemical adhesives into temporary constructions. As an Interact action, you can attach a [glue bomb](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3295) to the extruder.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** A glue bomb is installed in the extruder; **Effect** The extruder converts the glue bomb into a 30-foot [rope](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2748), [whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=404), or [net](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2738), depending on the nozzle die you choose when activating the device. The created object lasts for 1 hour. The DC to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) a created rope (if used to bind a creature) or net is equal to the consumed glue bomb’s DC and Escaping destroys the created object.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Claws of the Tyrant</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Claws of the Tyrant](/Sources.aspx?ID=266) pg. 110

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The _Spleen Bloodstone of Arazni_ represents freedom. Holding the _Spleen Bloodstone_ makes you feel as if no bonds can contain you.

**Activate—Sure Footing** <actions string="Single Action to Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;  **Requirements** You aren’t [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81); **Effect** You [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) or [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305), treating both [difficult and greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) as normal terrain during the movement. For each additional action you spend, you can Step or Stride again with the same benefits. If you have a [climb](/Rules.aspx?ID=2349) or [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350), you can instead Climb or Fly respectively.

**Activate—Break Bonds** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You worship [Arazni](/Deities.aspx?ID=326) or are favored by her; **Effect** The [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=63), [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64), [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77), [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=87), and [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) conditions, as well as any Speed penalties affecting you, immediately end unless the effect is [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644) and of 12th level or higher. You can use this ability even if your actions are restricted or otherwise decided for you (such as being confused or controlled).

**Destruction** If a worshipper of Arazni willingly gains the [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=64) condition or becomes [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) while holding the _Spleen Bloodstone_, the _Bloodstone_ explodes, dealing 10d6 [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610) damage to all creatures in a 20-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) (DC 28 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

May contain spoilers from Blood Lords **Source** [Pathfinder #185: A Taste of Ashes](/Sources.aspx?ID=188) pg. 78 **Price** 1,600 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands or mounted **Bulk** 3 --- This drum-shaped metal floodlight has a metal handle on each side and a housing at its base to be slotted into a stand or pedestal. A _splendid floodlight_ has a primary function as well as several secondary functions available by rotating through a series of translucent sheets called gels. A _splendid floodlight_ comes with the four gels described below, but other gels exist with different abilities. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per hour; **Requirements** The _splendid floodlight's_ light is off; **Effect** You flip a switch and the _splendid floodlight_ emits bright magical light in a 120-foot cone that hangs in the air and remains in place even if you move the floodlight. If the cone passes through an area of magical [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) or targets a creature affected by magical darkness, the splendid floodlight attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the darkness. Creatures in the cone who are [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) reduce the value of their frightened condition by 1 at the beginning of each turn they start in the area of the cone. The light remains in place until you Interact to flip the switch again to extinguish the floodlight. If you haven't done so after an hour, the switch flips on its own and the floodlight turns off. **Activate** Interact; **Requirements** The _splendid floodlight's_ light is on; **Effect** You rotate one of the following gels into position in the floodlight or rotate a gel out. You can do this even if the _splendid floodlight_ has been moved from its position when the light was created. You can have up to two gels in place at once; if you rotate in a third, another of your choice rotates out.
  • **Red Gel** The light lends an air of gravitas to all creatures illuminated by it. Creatures in the light gain a +2 item bonus to Charisma-based skill checks.
  • **Yellow Gel** [Invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) creatures and objects are visible while in the light, and creatures with the [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149) trait appear substantial rather than ghostly.
  • **Green Gel** All creatures illuminated by the light appear to be wearing exceptionally stylish clothing with elegantly coiffed hair styles.
  • **Blue Gel** [Undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creatures in the light appear as they did when alive, and living creatures in the light appear decayed, like an undead creature.

---

Splints can be applied to the following joints: finger, hand, wrist, elbow, knee, and shin. They are strapped to the desired area but are more rigid in structure than supports and braces, with metal or wooden bars pulled firmly against the bone structure to provide constant support (ring splints only attach to a single digit). They are a little less flexible, but you still have full use of your limbs and fingers when using one. You still have full mobility of the limb when not wearing it, but the limb becomes painful and feels less secure without the extra support it normally has, which might present physical symptoms.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 103

**Price** 360 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=436)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [hauling](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1372) [longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=436)_ is lined with the flesh of a fallen [hydra](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3064) and ornate carvings on the grip that depict the hydra’s number of heads it had before it was slain. When you wield the bow in combat, you regain 2 Hit Points at the start of each of your turns.

**Activate—Two-Headed Arrow** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You imbue your arrow with the properties of a hydra, splitting it in two and sending each at a different foe. Make two ranged [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), each against a separate target. Both targets must be in your line of sight, and within 50 feet of you. Both Strikes count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both attacks. Additionally, after using this ability, you do not regain Hit Points from wielding the bow on your next turn.

**Activate—Five-Headed Arrow** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You make a powerful [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) propelled by the ferocity of a hydra at a target within your first range increment. If your Strike is successful, the arrow deals damage as normal and then passes through the target, splitting into four pieces. Choose four other targets within 30 feet of the original target and make a single ranged Strike with your multiple attack penalty, comparing the result to each secondary target’s AC. After using this ability, you do not regain Hit Points from wielding the bow until after your next daily preparations.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the flesh from a severed head of a [hydra](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3064).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This flexible _+2 striking [sap](/Weapons.aspx?ID=37)_ is crafted from the stalks of cave fungi and bound around a mesh of spore-infused gills. Demon-worshipping [xulgaths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=102) use _spore saps_ to capture spellcasters alive for later sacrifice.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact ([poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Frequency** three times per day; **Trigger** You successfully Strike a creature with the _spore sap_;  **Effect** The _spore sap_ releases a puff of stupefying fungal spores. The target must succeed at a DC 28 Fortitude save or become [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 minute (stupefied 2 on a critical failure).

>
[Sportlebore Capsule](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3240)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Ingested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=633" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=669" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 111

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Onset** 1 minute

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tiny capsule of soluble material is filled with a flavorless clear powder mixed with thousands of microscopic eggs laid by insidious parasites known as sportlebores. If the capsule or its contents are swallowed by an unwitting victim, the eggs rapidly hatch inside their unfortunate host, causing great abdominal pain. The target can't recover from the poison's [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) or [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) condition except by magic. After stage 3, the target returns to stage 1, but if it progresses to stage 3 a second time, the damage is doubled.

**Saving Throw** DC 22 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 6 minutes; **Stage 1** sickened 1 (1 minute); **Stage 2** enfeebled 1 and sickened 1 (1 minute); **Stage 3** 4d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save) and enfeebled 2 as the affected target painfully vomits (1 minute)

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 7 Sportlebore Capsule Alchemical Consumable Ingested Poison Source Howl of the Wild pg. 111 Price 70 gp Onset 1 minute Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Single Action (manipulate) This tiny capsule of soluble material is filled with a flavorless clear powder mixed with thousands of microscopic eggs laid by insidious parasites known as sportlebores. A sparkling candy coating covers a sprite apple. For 10 minutes after consuming a sprite apple, you shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot emanation (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 20 feet). While shedding this light, you can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) if you're visible, and if you're [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), you're concealed instead rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39). The light matches the vibrant color of the apple's candy coating. Creatures in the bright light are subject to another effect, depending on the type of apple.

---

On the Elemental [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4), small clouds of differing colors can sometimes float separately from other cloud formations. Clever people can spin these clouds into small handfuls, creating a magical bundle of elemental power. Unlike most bottled breath, spun clouds don't have any effect on you while you hold them in your lungs, but you can exhale the cloud as a single action. When exhaled, the cloud flows out and expands into a 20-foot burst within 60 feet of you. The cloud dissipates after 1 minute.

[Spurned Lute](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2389)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 193

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Made of a deep-brown rosewood, a _spurned lute_ is adorned with carved flowers. The lute appears to be and functions as a [virtuoso instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37). (Other _spurned instruments_ exist, but the lute is the least rare.) This lute has a jealous streak, demanding total loyalty from its “partner” musician. After you play the lute for the first time, it fuses to you. If you go a day without using it to [Perform](/Actions.aspx?ID=59), you become [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) until you next do so. After that, when you attempt a [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) check using an instrument other than the lute, you take a –4 circumstance penalty to do so, and you must succeed at a DC 20 Will save or become stupefied 1 for 1 minute.

</column>

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 99 **Price** 160 gp **Usage** implanted --- Sacs full of dark ink have been implanted inside your mouth, allowing you to spit it forth. **Activate—Spray Ink** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You splatter ink in a 10-foot cone, covering creatures and revealing [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) ones. Each creature in the area must succeed at a DC 20 Reflex save or become covered in ink. If a creature has its invisibility negated by this ink, it is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) instead of invisible. A creature can negate the effects of the ink by spending two Interact actions to wipe off the ink. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target’s invisibility is negated for 2 rounds.
**Failure** The target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round. Its invisibility is negated for 1 minute.
**Critical Failure** The target is blinded for 10 minutes. Its invisibility is negated for 10 minutes. If this graft is used underwater, you can instead choose to release the ink in a 10-foot emanation. The resulting ink cloud lasts for 10 minutes. All creatures in the ink cloud become concealed, and all creatures outside the ink cloud become concealed to creatures within it.

A staff of arcane might is a _+1 striking [staff](/Traits.aspx?ID=151)_. **Activate—Sunder** ([death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Effect** You destroy the staff, unleashing a blast of arcane power in a 30- foot cone, dealing 2d6 force damage per charge remaining in the staff with a DC 30 basic Reflex save. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.   • **3rd** [_force barrage_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1536), [_paralyze_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1622)
  • **4th** [_dispelling globe_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1494), [_mystic armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1611), [_translocate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724)

  • **8th** mystic armor, wall of force
  • **9th** [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493), [_falling stars_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1521), howling blizzard

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 30 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- This white marble staff is carved into the figure of an abstract knight, its shield bearing the symbol of Lastwall, with a wickedly pointed sword made of dark wood raised high above its head. When you wield it as a weapon, it gains the [versatile P](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) trait and functions as a wooden stake, allowing you to use it to stake vampires, and your Strikes with the staff gain a +1 circumstance bonus to damage rolls against undead. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells. Staff of Final Rest **Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 30 **Price** 240 gp **Bulk** 1 ---
  • **Cantrip** [_disrupt undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=79)
  • **1st** [_disrupting weapons_](/Spells.aspx?ID=80), [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148)
  • **2nd** _heal_, [_gentle repose_](/Spells.aspx?ID=131)
Staff of Final Rest (Greater) **Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 30 **Price** 900 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The circumstance bonus to damage rolls is +2.
  • **3rd** [_bind undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=22), _disrupting weapons_, _heal_
  • **4th** _heal_, [_holy cascade_](/Spells.aspx?ID=151)
Staff of Final Rest (Major) **Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 30 **Price** 9,000 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The circumstance bonus to damage rolls is +3.
  • **5th** [_death ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=64), _disrupting weapons_, _heal_
  • **6th** [_field of life_](/Spells.aspx?ID=114), _heal_, _holy cascade_
  • **7th** _heal_, _holy cascade_, [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=326)

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 308 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- This bizarre staff is made from oak, capped with a cluster of eye-shaped gemstones that seem to move and undulate at the corner of your vision. While wielding the staff, you can peer through the eyes on the staff rather than your own, using your normal visual senses (including any benefits of spells like [_see the unseen_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1663)). You can maneuver the staff to see things around corners, at higher elevations, or in places where the staff can fit but your head can't. This doesn't provide sufficient line of effect to target creatures around corners. The eyes are as vulnerable as your eyes and can be affected by anything that alters your vision, such as a blinding flash of light. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. **Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells. <traits>

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bizarre staff is made from oak, capped with a cluster of eye-shaped gemstones that seem to move and undulate at the corner of your vision. While wielding the staff, you can peer through the eyes, using your normal visual senses (including any benefits of spells affecting your vision, like [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271)). You can maneuver the staff to see things around corners, at higher elevations, or in places where the staff can fit but your head can't. This doesn't provide sufficient line of effect to target creatures around corners. The eyes are as vulnerable as your eyes and can be affected by anything that alters your vision, such as a blinding flash of light.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;     **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells.

</column>

fields.text: Item 6+ Staff of Impossible Visions Uncommon Magical Staff Source Player Core 2 pg. 308 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 This bizarre staff is made from oak, capped with a cluster of eye-shaped gemstones that seem to move and undulate at the corner of your vision. While wielding the staff, you can peer through the eyes on the staff rather than your own, using your normal visual senses (including any benefits of spells like see the unseen ). You can maneuver the staff to see things around corners, at higher elevations, or in places where the staff can fit but your head can't. This doesn't provide sufficient line of effect to target creatures around corners. The eyes are as vulnerable as your eyes and can be affected by anything that alters your vision, such as a blinding flash of light. Activate Cast a Spell; Effect You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list. Craft Requirements Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells. **Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 595 **Price** 10,000 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- This staff of magically hardened wood is topped with a silver sculpture depicting magical runic symbols. When used as a weapon, a staff of power is a +2 greater striking staff. Voluntarily destroying a staff of power unleashes an incredible blast of energy. When wielding the staff, you can Interact to break it. This releases a 30-foot-burst magical explosion centered on the staff. This deals 2d8 force damage per charge remaining in the staff (DC 40 basic Reflex save). You automatically critically fail your save. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies instantly; this is a death effect. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.
  • **1st** [_ray of enfeeblement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=244)
  • **2nd** [_continual flame_](/Spells.aspx?ID=50)
  • **3rd** [_levitate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=170)
  • **4th** [_globe of invulnerability_](/Spells.aspx?ID=137), [_paralyze_](/Spells.aspx?ID=213)
  • **5th** [_magic missile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=180)
  • **6th** [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=363)
  • **7th** [_cone of cold_](/Spells.aspx?ID=47), [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119), [_lightning bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=172)
**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells.

<row gap="medium">

---

A large, stylized symbol of an eye adorns the top of this wooden staff, representing the watchful eye of the divine powers. The bearer of the staff can guide and protect, seeing bounties and tragedies that could befall them in the future. When wielding this staff, you gain a +1 item bonus on [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) or [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=27), and to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26).

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;     **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 131

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Bo Staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=372)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Also known as _Ruyi Bang_, this [+3](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [major striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [greater extending](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2836) [grievous](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2841) [bo staff](/Weapons.aspx?ID=372) is a legendary artifact wielded by the Monkey King, [Sun Wukong](/Deities.aspx?ID=316). Unlike normal bo staves, the Staff of Sun Wukong is made of solid iron with two brilliant gold bands at either end.

**Activate—Meteor Slam** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You extend the staff with the force of a meteor, dealing 10d10 bludgeoning damage to a single creature within 120 feet and making it [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 for 1 day. All other creatures within 10 feet of the target (except the staff’s wielder) take 8d10 [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage (DC 43 basic Reflex save).

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> Close at Hand;     **Effect** It’s said that Sun Wukong tucked this magical staff behind his ear during his travels. When not in use, the Staff of Sun Wukong shrinks to the size and weight of a needle or toothpick, making it highly concealable (+4 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to hide it from sight). In this form, the item has negligible Bulk. You can [Activate](/Actions.aspx?ID=100) this ability again to return the staff to its normal size.

**Activate—Cloud Somersault** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You use the shapeshifting capabilities of this relic to propel yourself great distances. You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) up to 50 feet in any direction.

**Destruction** Despite being made of iron and gold, mundane heat sources can’t damage the Staff of Sun Wukong. Magical fire similarly has no effect on this relic. The only way to destroy this item is to expose it to the intense heat of a specific volcano in the depths of the Songil Sea (though which volcano remains shrouded in myth).

</column>

**7th** [_blightburn blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=651), [_control sand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=652), [_unfettered pack_](/Spells.aspx?ID=350)

  • **Cantrip** [_know direction_](/Spells.aspx?ID=169)
  • **1st** [_create water_](/Spells.aspx?ID=53), [_pass without trace_](/Spells.aspx?ID=215)
  • **2nd** [_endure elements_](/Spells.aspx?ID=99), [_enhance victuals_](/Spells.aspx?ID=101)
Staff of the Desert Winds (Greater) **Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 190 **Price** 1,750 gp **Bulk** 1 ---
  • **3rd** [_remove disease_](/Spells.aspx?ID=251), [_wall of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=367)
  • **4th** [_air walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=6)
  • **5th** [_elemental form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=98)

  • **6rd** [_flesh to stone_](/Spells.aspx?ID=123), [_stone to flesh_](/Spells.aspx?ID=311)
  • **7th** [_fiery body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=115)

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 595 **Price** 90,000 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Sigils and runes of ancient and powerful magic cover the iron cladding on this long wooden staff. A staff of the magi is a +3 major striking staff, and when wielding it you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells. Voluntarily destroying a staff of the magi unleashes a truly devastating wave of arcane energy that surges out, dissipating with distance. When wielding the staff, you can break it using an Interact action. This releases a 30-foot‑burst magical explosion centered on the staff. This deals 2d10 force damage per charge remaining in the staff (DC 40 basic Reflex save), You automatically critically fail your save. The explosion continues to echo beyond the initial blast zone, dealing half as much damage to creatures beyond 30 feet but within a 60-foot burst. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies instantly; this is a death effect. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.
  • **Cantrip** [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66), [_light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=171), [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), [_telekinetic projectile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=334)
  • **1st** [_lock_](/Spells.aspx?ID=174)
  • **2nd** [_enlarge_](/Spells.aspx?ID=102), [_glitterdust_](/Spells.aspx?ID=136), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [_knock_](/Spells.aspx?ID=168), [_telekinetic maneuver_](/Spells.aspx?ID=333), [_web_](/Spells.aspx?ID=374)
  • **3rd** [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78), [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119), [_lightning bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=172)
  • **4th** _invisibility_, _enlarge_, _fireball_, [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362), _web_
  • **5th** [_cone of cold_](/Spells.aspx?ID=47), [_passwall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=216), [_telekinetic haul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=332)
  • **6th** [_disintegrate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=76), _dispel magic_, _fireball_, _lightning bolt_
  • **7th** _cone of cold_, _passwall_, [_plane shift_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222), _wall of fire_
  • **8th** _fireball_, [_mage armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=176)
  • **9th** _dispel magic_, [_meteor swarm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=191), [_summon dragon_](/Spells.aspx?ID=319)
**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells.

---

This magically reinforced [wooden shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=2) (Hardness 6, HP 36, BT 18) normally has a blank face. It can absorb a [staff](/Equipment.aspx?Category=32) and transform between a shield and staff. When you prepare a staff, you can hold it up to the shield, at which point the items will merge, and the shield's face becomes an image corresponding to the type of magic, such as a skull for a [_staff of necromancy_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=360).

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You change the _staff-storing shield_ from its shield form into the stored staff, which has an image of the shield on it, or change it from the stored staff back into a shield.

It can absorb a staff and transform between a shield and staff. When you prepare a staff, you can hold it up to the shield, at which point the items merge until your next [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), and the shield’s face becomes an image corresponding to the type of magic, such as a skull for a _[staff of the dead](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3047)_.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Stag's Helm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1752)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 589

**Price** 240 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This impressive-looking helmet is crafted to resemble the skull of a mighty stag. Although made from bone, the antlers and helm are as strong as iron. While the Stag Lord himself wears this helmet in the Kingmaker Adventure Path, _stag's helms_ are actually the creation of the church of [Erastil](/Deities.aspx?ID=6), and worshipers of this deity find that the helm is not only particularly comfortable to wear, but that they can activate it once per hour rather than once per day.

 Rather than restrict the senses, a _stag's helm_ enhances them, causing the world to appear in more vibrant colors and significantly enhancing the ambient sounds of the region without making them distracting. While worn, it grants a +1 item bonus to Perception checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" />  ;  **Frequency** once per day (or once per hour if the wearer worships Erastil);   **Effect** Choose a single creature within 30 feet. The _stag's helm_ focuses your aim and grants supernatural insight into your next shot. Your target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to the next ranged Strike you make this turn against them.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Stage Fright Missive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2066)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Curse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=38" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Missive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=485" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 85

**Price** 22 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Composing a _stage fright missive_ usually involves creating a scathing review, insulting letter, or embarrassing image that ridicules the recipient. The activating creature must succeed at a DC 20 Will save or be overcome with embarrassment for 1 hour, taking a –1 status penalty to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks. During this time, if the creature attempts to speak or perform in front of an audience, they become [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34). When they recover from this sickened condition, the missive's effects end. You choose when composing the missive whether it remains as a non-magical document or burns to ash after imparting its magic.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Curse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=38" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />

<trait label="Missive" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=485" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 85

**Price** 22 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>envision, Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Composing a _stage fright missive_ usually involves creating a scathing review, insulting letter, or embarrassing image that ridicules the recipient. The activating creature must succeed at a DC 20 Will save or be overcome with embarrassment for 1 hour, taking a –1 status penalty to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks. During this time, if the creature attempts to speak or perform in front of an audience, they become [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1. When they recover from this sickened condition, the missive’s effects end. You choose when composing the missive whether it remains as a non‑magical document or burns to ash after imparting its magic.

    level="1"

    pfs="Limited"
>
[Stage Magician's Cloak](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3634)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Curtain Call</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 81

**Price** 3,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn cloak

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black velvet cloak has a silvery blue iridescent lining. The cloak can be worn with either side facing out—switching from one side to the other requires two Interact actions. If these actions are both taken on the same turn, the act of removing and redonning the cloak doesn’t cause it to lose its [investiture](/Rules.aspx?ID=3163). When worn with the black velvet lining facing out, the _stage magician’s cloak_ grants a +2 item bonus to [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) checks. When worn with the silvery blue lining facing out, it grants a +2 item bonus to [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) checks. 

**Activate—Now You See Me...** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Distracting colorful smoke blasts outward from the cloak in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387), causing all creatures in the area to become [off‑guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn (DC 30 Will save). If you were previously [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96), you lose those conditions. You become [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) for 1 round and may use the extra action to [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297), [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306), or [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305).

**Activate—...Now You Don't** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=710)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Harmless silver smoke issues from the cloak in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). You cast a 2nd-rank [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1577) on yourself and are transported, along with all items you’re wearing and holding, from your current space to an unoccupied space within 30 feet that you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you’re carrying it in an extradimensional space—the transportation part of this effect fails.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Earth" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=55" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 100

**Price** 60 gp

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You can throw a _stalagmite seed_, use it as a sling stone, or pack it into firearm ammunition. When you use the seed, you aim it at a 5-foot square rather than a specific target. Stalagmites of assorted sizes erupt in the square the seed lands in, dealing 6d6 piercing damage to any creature within that space (DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The stalagmites remain for 1 minute, creating [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) in that space, before they crumble into dust.

These black leather goggle frames have no lenses. Instead, when a character puts them on and invests them, the wearer's eyes transform and lengthen into snail-like eyestalks. The wobbly eyestalks stretch out through the lens holes and up over the wearer's head on lengthened optic nerves.

[Stalk Goggles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4024)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Morph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=113" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gatewalkers (Hardcover)](/Sources.aspx?ID=290) pg. 230

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These black leather goggle frames have no lenses. Instead, when a character puts them on and invests them, the wearer’s eyes transform and lengthen into snail-like eyestalks. The wobbly eyestalks stretch out through the lens holes and up over the wearer’s head on lengthened optic nerves.

**Activate—Looksee** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** By focusing hard, you can watch for enemies in all directions. You gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49) for 1 minute; during this time, you can’t be [flanked](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375).

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 300 **Price** 15 gp --- This snare explodes in a burst of cloying powder that can cling to a creature stepping into its square. A creature that enters the square of a stalker bane snare must attempt a DC 20 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** Powder sticks to the target, causing it to leave behind telltale footprints. Being [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) makes the target [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), rather than [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96), to creatures that could see it if it weren't invisible.
**Failure** Powder clumps on the target, constantly flaking away. Being invisible makes the target concealed, rather than hidden or undetected, to creatures that could see it if it weren't invisible.
**Critical Failure** As failure, and the creature is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) until the end of its next turn.

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed or held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This magical banner mimics the rich green of summer grass. While holding a _stalwart’s banner_, you can use the following ability.

**Activate—Stand Firm** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** You and allies within your banner’s aura gain 5 [temporary Hit Points](/Rules.aspx?ID=2321) and a +1 status bonus to your Fortitude DC and Reflex DC against any effect that would move you or knock you [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). These effects last for 1 round.

fields.text: Item 7+ Stalwart's Banner Uncommon Aura Magical Source Battlecry! pg. 140 Usage affixed or held in 1 hand Bulk L This magical banner mimics the rich green of summer grass. While holding a stalwart’s banner , you can use the following ability. Activate—Stand Firm Single Action (concentrate) Frequency once per minute; Effect You and allies within your banner’s aura gain 5 temporary Hit Points and a +1 status bonus to your Fortitude DC and Reflex DC against any effect that would move you or knock you prone. These effects last for 1 round. Item 7 Stalwart’s Banner Source Battlecry! pg. 140 Price 360 gp Item 12 Greater Stalwart’s Banner Source Battlecry! pg. 140 Price 2,000 gp The temporary Hit Points gained increase to 10, and the status bonus increases to +2. Item 17 Major Stalwart’s Banner Source Battlecry! pg. 140 Price 15,000 gp The temporary Hit Points gained increase to 15, and the status bonus increases to +3.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from The Fall of Plaguestone</spoilers>

---

This fairly simple ring has no gemstone inlaid, but the band is cast to resembled a fanged wolf’s head. Once per day, during your daily preparations, you can meditate on this ring to grant yourself 5 temporary Hit Points. These last until your next daily preparation, as long as you are wearing the ring.

>
[Stampede Medallion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1080)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 190

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon's heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon Concentrates on the medallion and their connection to you, allowing them to momentarily manifest into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an emanation around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon's Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Stampede Medallion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5189)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Eidolon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=386" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 245

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When crafted, a _stampede medallion_ looks like nothing more than small silver disk, about the same size as a silver piece. When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny, bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon’s heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382). 

**Activate—Impossible Tide** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon momentarily manifests into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon’s Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

</column>

<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 190

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When you invest this medallion for your eidolon, it changes shape to appear as a tiny bejeweled facsimile of the eidolon, magically attached just over your eidolon's heart. While your eidolon wears the medallion, they gain a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your eidolon Concentrates on the medallion and their connection to you, allowing them to momentarily manifest into a stampede of dozens of copies of themself. The stampede rampages out in every direction, swerving around your allies while trampling any foe on the ground in an emanation around your eidolon with a radius equal to your eidolon's Speed. Each of these foes takes 8d6 bludgeoning damage, with a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. On a critical failure, the foe is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). After dealing damage, the stampede of eidolons vanishes as quickly as it appeared.

Astrolabes can be used for navigation in unfamiliar or featureless locations. To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49). By spending 1 minute to measure the height of the stars and planets, a holder who knows the time and date can determine the latitude, and a holder who knows their latitude can determine the date and time. An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies. A standard astrolabe functions only on steady ground.

These standards are always constructed from uncut wood and a leather banner painted with the visage of a snarling beast—a wolf, boar, bear, lion, dragon, or similarly imposing creature. And while it might become lost on a battlefield scattered with gaudier standards, its effect bolsters those around a competent leader. When carrying this banner, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks and initiative rolls, and creatures in a 20-foot emanation also gain a +1 item bonus to initiative checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** An ally within 20 feet of you critically hits with a Strike; **Requirements** You have the [Battle Cry](/Feats.aspx?ID=759) skill feat; **Effect** You attempt to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) the foe the Strike hit.

May contain spoilers from Dead God's Hand **Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 142 --- Throneglass is an incredibly rare resource created during the violence of Earthfall 10,000 years ago, when the impact of falling stars enhanced certain shattered panes of green glass built into the architecture of important buildings in Azlant— particularly the Imperial Palace. As a material, throneglass is as strong as steel, but the ancient methods of crafting it into weapons have long been lost. Low-grade throneglass offers no additional benefit to a weapon crafted from it other than the cosmetic and intrinsic value of the precious material, but standard-grade and high-grade throneglass can retain psychic power and then release it through a strike. When a creature wielding a standard-grade or high-grade throneglass weapon succeeds at a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effect, the weapon stores some of that energy and holds it for a future attack. A standard-grade weapon can hold this energy for 1 round before it dissipates harmlessly, while a high-grade one can hold the energy for 1 minute. The next time you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) a creature with a throneglass weapon with stored energy, the creature struck must attempt a Will save (DC 24 for standardgrade throneglass, or DC 35 for high-grade throneglass) to avoid becoming [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 round (or stupefied 2 on a critical failure). ## Throneglass Items

---

This tattoo consists of numerous asterisks at regular intervals along the fingers of one hand, perfect for measuring stars against the horizon. When used against a clear night sky, the tattoo grants a +2 circumstance bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=64) and counts as a [compass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=16) for the purpose of that action.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact ([divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [metamagic](/Traits.aspx?ID=107)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The dots of the tattoo turn to points of light and fly above the head of a creature within 30 feet, where they form a three-star constellation that guides your spells further than they could normally travel. The constellation sheds dim light and remains visible even if the creature hides, aiding in locating it. Furthermore, while the constellation lasts, if you Cast a Spell that has a range and that spell would affect only the marked creature, the spell's range is increased by 30 feet. As is standard for increasing spell ranges, if the spell normally has a range of touch, you extend its range to 30 feet. Each time you use this benefit, one of the stars above the creature's head winks out; when all three have winked out or after 1 minute has passed, the effect ends.

These unusual gunpowder bombs, typically marked with a symbol of a four-pointed star on their outer surface, explode outward in the shape of a cross whenever they Strike a target. When you throw a star grenade, arrange two perpendicular 25-foot lines over the target, both centered on the target and moving straight through the target, not diagonally. Creatures other than the target within these two lines take [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage (typically 8 squares take splash damage for a Medium creature). Any effect that alters or adjusts the splash area's shape or size, like the alchemist feat [Expanded Splash](/Feats.aspx?ID=109), doesn't apply to star grenades.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #189: Dreamers of the Nameless Spires](/Sources.aspx?ID=195) pg. 77

**Price** 175 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You attempt a Will save against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) spell, but you haven't rolled yet

**Requirement** You have master proficiency in Will saves.
</row>

</column>

---

Found throughout Golarion, these star-shaped talismans of whalebone scrimshaw are carved by Erutaki from the Crown of the World. They are popular with adherents to the cult of [Desna](/Deities.aspx?ID=5), who believe the talismans protect their dreams.

 When you activate this talisman, you gain a +2 status bonus to saves against enchantment magic with the mental trait for 1 minute. On the triggering save, if the outcome of the roll is a failure, you get a success instead, or if the outcome is a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

</column>

[Starfall Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1861)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 22

**Price** 23,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Heavy Rondache](/Shields.aspx?ID=10)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This [high-grade adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=310) [heavy rondache](/Shields.aspx?ID=10) (Hardness 17, HP  100, BT 50) bears a _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41)_ and has dents that resemble craters on its surface. While wielding the shield, you have fire resistance 15.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You Stride up to three times. This movement doesn't trigger reactions and ignores difficult terrain. At the end of your movement, you deal 6d10 bludgeoning damage in a 10-foot emanation and 14d6 fire damage in a 40-foot emanation (DC 40 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save, with the results applying to both the bludgeoning and fire damage). The space where you end your movement and all adjacent spaces become difficult terrain for 1 minute, and the shield glows red-hot for 10 minutes, during which it gains the effect of the [_greater flaming_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295) property rune.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 24"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Starfaring Cloak](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2366)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 180

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The swirling folds of a _starfaring cloak_ appear to contain the night sky, with the stars rotating hypnotically through its firmament shedding dim light to a range of 10 feet. While wearing the cloak, you gain a +10-foot item bonus to your Speed and a fly Speed equal to your Speed. You can survive comfortably without breathing, in the void of space, and in [severe or extreme cold or heat](/Rules.aspx?ID=642). Also, you gain sustenance from starlight and sunlight, so if you're outdoors for an hour or more per day, you don't need to eat or drink. While wearing the cloak, you can navigate perfectly and unerringly by looking up at the sky.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) ,[fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You make an attack roll, skill check, or saving throw;  **Effect** Reroll the triggering roll and take the higher result. This is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The cloak casts [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=288) at 4th rank (DC 42).

---

When you invest this [_clear quartz crystal ball_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=253), it orbits your head like an [_aeon stone_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407). As long as you have the _stargazer_ invested, you can use an Interact action to direct it to orbit one of your hands where you can telekinetically smash the orb into foes, wielding it as a _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)_. While you're directing the _stargazer_, your hand is full, and you can send it back to your head with another Interact action. On a critical hit, the _stargazer_ pulses with hypnotic starlight, [dazzling](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) the struck creature for 1 round. A stargazer doesn't add [critical specialization effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=235).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 122

**Price** 550 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tattoo usually depicts a humanoid skull with staring eyes in its sockets, but any creature with two eyes and a skull is possible, such as a [wolf](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=101), [phoenix](/Monsters.aspx?ID=330), or [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83). When your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) condition increases to a value that would kill you, this tattoo reduces your dying value to 1 fewer than would kill you. If a [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effect would kill you—provided the effect is from a creature of 8th level or lower or a spell of 4th rank or lower—this tattoo activates and keeps you alive instead. You can benefit from this ability only once per day. Each time the tattoo prevents you from dying, one of its eyes disappears, the image now featuring either an empty socket or an eyepatch or other covering. After both eyes vanish, the tattoo becomes non-magical and no longer protects you. If you receive a new _staring skull_ tattoo, any other you have loses its staring eyes and becomes non-magical.

</column>

fields.text: Item 8 Staring Skull Abjuration Invested Magical Tattoo Source Treasure Vault pg. 122 Price 550 gp Usage tattooed on the body This tattoo usually depicts a humanoid skull with staring eyes in its sockets, but any creature with two eyes and a skull is possible, such as a wolf, phoenix, or psychopomp. When your dying condition increases to a value that would kill you, this tattoo reduces your dying value to 1 fewer than would kill you. If a death effect would kill you—provided the effect is from a creature of 8th level or lower or a spell of 4th level or lower—this tattoo activates and keeps you alive instead. You can benefit from this ability only once per day. Each time the tattoo prevents you from dying, one of its eyes disappears, the image now featuring either an empty socket or an eyepatch or other covering. After both eyes vanish, the tattoo becomes non-magical and no longer protects you. If you receive a new staring skull tattoo, any other you have loses its staring eyes and becomes non-magical.

May contain spoilers from Malevolence **Source** [Malevolence](/Sources.aspx?ID=88) pg. 67 **Price** 650 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- Even during the time of Thassilon, when the Order of the Starless Night still existed, _starless scopes_ were uncommon. Today, this final scope might well be the last one to survive the passage of time. A _starless scope_ is a handheld telescope crafted of silver and fine wood. When one peers at the sky through a _starless scope_, one always views the sky as if during a clear night. A starless scope adds a +2 item bonus to [Astronomy Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) and Perception checks made to observe the skies, as it causes all celestial objects to dim when not directly observed, allowing its user to more easily observe their intended subject. It also grants a +2 item bonus to all [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) checks made to [Identify Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24). A starless scope also functions as a divine focus for worshipers of [Desna](/Deities.aspx?ID=5). The magic of a starless scope requires a specially prepared lens to function, and it's possible to shatter the lens if you roll poorly when activating the _starless scope_. Without a functional lens, a _starless scope_ doesn't function. You can replace a shattered lens with a functional lens by taking a two-action activity with the manipulate trait. If you know the formula for the starless scope, you can [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) a new lens with a DC 25 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) (master) check. A starless scope lens is a level 9 item worth 100 gp. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** you use the _starless scope_ as a divine focus; **Requirements** you worship Desna; **Effect** You attempt to enhance the effects of a spell as you cast it by attempting a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check against the spell's DC, as determined by [Table 10–5](/Rules.aspx?ID=554) **Critical Success** Any attack rolls you make with the spell gain a +2 status bonus, and any saving throw a foe makes against the spell takes a –2 status penalty. If you would normally cast the spell from a spell slot, and the spell is 5th level or lower, you don't spend the spell slot and cast the spell from the _starless scope_ instead.
**Success** Any attack rolls you make with the spell gain a +1 status bonus, and any saving throw a foe makes against the spell takes a –1 status penalty.
**Failure** The spell is cast normally. Attempt a DC 11 flat check. On a failure, the _starless scope's_ lens shatters.
**Critical Failure** The spell is disrupted and the _starless scope's_ lens shatters. **Activate** Interact ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** You raise the scope to your eye and observe a creature within 30 feet. You can attempt to identify the creature by [Recalling Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). The _starless scope_ adds a +2 item bonus to this check. If the creature is associated with the Dominion of the Black or the Elder Mythos, or is a creature whose actions have blasphemed against Desna (Ioseff Xarwin's ghost falls into this latter category), the creature must attempt a DC 27 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected, and the _starless scope's_ lens shatters.
**Success** The creature shines with starlight for 1 round. During this time, the creature can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) if it is visible. If it's [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), it's concealed rather than being [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39). The creature takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws against [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) effects while it shimmers with starlight.
**Failure** As success, but the creature also suffers an additional effect. An [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creature loses its incorporeal trait as long as it shines with starlight. Any other creature becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) as long as it shines with starlight.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the duration of the starlight is 1 minute, and the status penalty to saving throws against divine effects increases to –2.
