A liquid with the appearance of an expressive night sky and a taste that’s sheer pleasure, _starsong nectar_ grants you cheerful confidence and incredible luck for 10 minutes after you drink it. However, if you show too much caution at any point during this time (GM’s discretion), you must succeed at a DC 6 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) or the potion’s effects end. While the potion lasts, you gain a +3 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks, and you aren’t [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to creatures due to them [flanking](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375) you or being [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) from or undetected by you. You are temporarily immune to this potion for 24 hours once its effects end.

While the potion lasts, though, if you take a moment to imagine the future, you choose the best courses of action. This aspect of the potion grants you the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** Until the start of your next turn, roll two d20s for any attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks you make and take the higher result.

While the potion lasts, you gain a +3 status bonus to attack rolls, initiative rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks, and you aren’t [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96) creatures or when [flanked](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375). You are temporarily immune to this potion for 24 hours once its effects end.

While the potion lasts, though, if you take a moment to imagine the future, you choose the best courses of action. This aspect of the potion grants you the following activation.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per round;   **Effect** Until the start of your next turn, roll two d20s for any attack rolls, Perception checks, saving throws, and skill checks you make and take the higher result.

This hefty winch is powered by a small steam engine and includes a 100 ft. length of steel cable, which enables you to haul a heavier load than you could with a hand cranked winch or [comealong](/Equipment.aspx?ID=865). A steam winch allows you to slowly pull a heavy load (usually up to 50 Bulk) along a flat surface or up and down a vertical expanse.

 Attaching a steam winch to a device takes three Interact actions, while starting the winch (and getting it warm enough to operate) takes 10 minutes. Once in operation, a steam winch requires regular maintenance to function. Every twenty minutes, the boiler must be refilled and heat levels maintained.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
<trait label="Steam" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=415" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 89

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 6,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn backpack

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

---

The steamflight pack allows its user to fly without using magic or wings. Each steamflight pack looks like a large brass backpack with two large nozzles mounted on the sides pointing downward. It also features metal arms reaching around the front that terminate in handles with activation buttons on them. When the user holds down an activation button, a complex series of mechanisms pumps water from the large tank in the backpack and releases it through the nozzles as powerful jets of steam, enabling the user to fly short distances. Tilting the handle adjusts the nozzles' angles, allowing the user to control the direction of their flight.

 When active, the steamflight pack gives the user a fly Speed of 20 feet. It carries enough water for 20 minutes of operation and can be refilled in five minutes with a supply of normal water and a funnel.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You turn the steamflight pack on or off.

Each steamflight pack looks like a large brass backpack with two large nozzles mounted on the sides pointing downward. It also features metal arms reaching around the front that terminate in handles with activation buttons on them. When the user holds down an activation button, a complex series of mechanisms pumps water from the large tank in the backpack and releases it through the nozzles as powerful jets of steam, enabling the user to fly short distances. Tilting the handle adjusts the nozzles' angles, allowing the user to control the direction of their flight. When active, the steamflight pack gives the user a fly Speed of 20 feet. It carries enough water for 20 minutes of operation and can be refilled in five minutes with a supply of normal water and a funnel. Activate Two Actions (manipulate) Effect You turn the steamflight pack on or off.

---

This carved iron cloud appears unfinished and full of spurs, blemishes, and other imperfections. When used as a catalyst to cast a _[_weapon storm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1758)_ spell, the caster’s weapon propels them forward. Before choosing the spell’s area, [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to twice your Speed. This movement must be in a straight [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388) and doesn’t trigger reactions. The spell is then cast from your new location.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Wake the Dead #5](/Sources.aspx?ID=220) pg. 25 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**Interact or Strike --- A viscous acidic goo fills this glass vial, specially designed to eat through metallic objects. You can throw the steelscour as an alchemical bomb, target a metal creature or metal object held by a creature. Steelscour has no effect on living or undead flesh, and deals half damage to objects constructed of non-metal materials.
Instead of using steelscour as a bomb, you can pour it on an adjacent unattended metal object with an Interact action, automatically dealing the listed [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) for 5 rounds with not flat check to end the condition. When used this way, steelscour loses the bomb trait. Steelscour (lesser) **Source** [Wake the Dead #5](/Sources.aspx?ID=220) pg. 25 **Price** 3 gp --- It deals 1d8 persistent acid damage that ignores up to 5 hardness from metal. Steelscour (moderate) **Source** [Wake the Dead #5](/Sources.aspx?ID=220) pg. 25 **Price** 9 gp --- You gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls. It deals 2d8 persistent acid damage that ignores up to 5 hardness from metal. Steelscour (greater) **Source** [Wake the Dead #5](/Sources.aspx?ID=220) pg. 25 **Price** 215 gp --- You gain a +2 item bonus to attack rolls. It deals 3d8 persistent acid damage that ignores up to 10 hardness from metal. Steelscour (major) **Source** [Wake the Dead #5](/Sources.aspx?ID=220) pg. 25 **Price** 210 gp --- You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls. It deals 4d8 persistent acid damage that ignores up to 15 hardness from metal.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 171

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** round

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row><actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A series of small stone discs pressed into a single round make up this ammunition. When you fire an activated _stepping stone shot_, whether you hit or miss your target, the shot creates a series of supports in a line that creatures can walk on as if solid ground. The line can ascend or descend at a 45-degree angle. The discs support any amount of weight, but don't otherwise pose any sort of obstacle; creatures and attacks can move through them if they wish. They crumble to dust if anything attempts to move or otherwise manipulate them. A creature can use a two-action activity, which has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) trait, to Stride up to its speed on the stones while causing them to crumble behind it. This ammunition does not work in firearms with the [scatter](/Traits.aspx?ID=413) trait. The maximum length of the line depends on the type of ammunition. However, the line also can't extend beyond the maximum distance for a Strike from your firearm (usually six times the firearm's range increment).

</column>

The line can ascend or descend at a 45-degree angle. The discs support any amount of weight, but don’t otherwise pose any sort of obstacle; creatures and attacks can move through them if they wish. They crumble to dust if anything attempts to move or otherwise manipulate them. A creature can use a two-action activity, which has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait, to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) up to its speed on the stones while causing them to crumble behind it. This ammunition does not work in firearms with the [scatter](/Traits.aspx?ID=848) trait. The maximum length of the line depends on the type of ammunition. However, the line also can’t extend beyond the maximum distance for a Strike from your firearm (usually six times the firearm’s range increment).

These bombs have been mixed with sticky algae that glow and emit poison. Attacks with this bomb don't take the normal penalties and restrictions for being used in water or underwater. The DC to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) a creature using this trail is 19, but the trail appears only in water.

---

Woven from swaths of rich brocade silk and embroidered with ancient Azlanti script in golden thread, this stole imparts a noble appearance to even the homeliest of individuals when draped over the shoulders. While wearing a stole of civility, you receive a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) with humans or [Make a Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) of humans, and a +2 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks against humans. The stole also grants you full understanding of the [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49) language.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** you are a human; **Effect** You gain 10 temporary Hit Points, which last for 10 minutes.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 169 --- Stone was one of the earliest materials used to create tools, and crafters can still fashion it into a variety of implements, weapons, and even armor. Simple stone objects are made from common materials such as flint or basalt, while exquisite stone objects might be made from crystal, obsidian, or semi-precious gems. Particularly notable stone armors or weapons might even be crafted entirely from a giant emerald, ruby, or sapphire, though they can still use the base statistics presented below. Stone can replace the striking surface of any melee weapon as long as it has no complex moving parts, and ammunition can be crafted with it. Stone can replace metal components in [chain](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=1) and [composite](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=2) armor; only [plate](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=5) armor that specifically describes itself as being made from stone can be crafted from this material ## Stone Objects

    level="1"
    right="Item 10+"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Stone Circle](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1295)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Structure" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=153" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 38

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk**  when not activated
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _stone circle_ appears to be a thumb-sized rectangular gray stone until activated.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> (1 minute) envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** When the circle is stood on the ground and activated, the stone grows into a massive stone pillar 13 feet high, 7 feet across, and weighing 25 tons. Identical pillars rise up from the ground marking a circle 100 feet across, with capstones connecting the pillars. There must be enough space to deploy the circle or it won't activate. During the activation, you align the _stone circle_ to face a single astronomical feature, such as the sun, the moon, or a constellation. You can revert the _stone circle_ back to its original state by using an Interact action to push over the original stone pillar. Once you do, the rest of the _stone circle_ collapses in a dramatic fashion, the stones falling, cracking, and disintegrating into dust. If you don't begin a ritual inside of the _stone circle_ within 1 day of its activation, it reverts back to its original state.

 When you cast a ritual of 5th level or lower within the _stone circle_, the first failure on a secondary check is improved by one degree of success (a critical failure becomes a failure and a failure becomes a success). Once you complete a ritual within the _stone circle_, regardless of the result, the stones collapse and it reverts back to its original form.

</column>

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 169 --- Stone was one of the earliest materials used to create tools, and crafters can still fashion it into a variety of implements, weapons, and even armor. Simple stone objects are made from common materials such as flint or basalt, while exquisite stone objects might be made from crystal, obsidian, or semi-precious gems. Particularly notable stone armors or weapons might even be crafted entirely from a giant emerald, ruby, or sapphire, though they can still use the base statistics presented below. Stone can replace the striking surface of any melee weapon as long as it has no complex moving parts, and ammunition can be crafted with it. Stone can replace metal components in [chain](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=1) and [composite](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=2) armor; only [plate](/ArmorGroups.aspx?ID=5) armor that specifically describes itself as being made from stone can be crafted from this material ## Stone Objects

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 87

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

**Access** Second-mark members of the Firebrands have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This smooth, round, gray stone fits neatly into the palm of your hand and feels comfortable to hold regardless of the size or shape of your hand. While you're holding the stone, it telepathically speaks to you at regular intervals in generic words of encouragement, such as “You can do it!” and “Let's go!” The encouraging words manifest in the voice of your internal monologue or take on the characteristics of the voice of someone you trust. Despite the similarity, you're aware that the stone is telepathically projecting its voice and can differentiate between the stone's voice and your internal monologue or the voice of the person you trust.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask the stone for help with a task. It speaks a few motivating words related to the task at hand, which grants you a +1 item bonus to the first skill check you attempt within 1 minute. You become temporarily immune to the effects of all _stones of encouragement_, even ones other than the one you activated, for 1 day. You can still hear the encouraging words of different stones if you hold them, but they don't provide any benefits.

---

This smooth, round, gray stone fits neatly into the palm of your hand and feels comfortable to hold regardless of the size or shape of your hand. While you're holding the stone, it telepathically speaks to you at regular intervals in generic words of encouragement, such as “You can do it!” and “Let's go!” The encouraging words manifest in the voice of your internal monologue or take on the characteristics of the voice of someone you trust. Despite the similarity, you're aware that the stone is telepathically projecting its voice and can differentiate between the stone's voice and your internal monologue or the voice of the person you trust.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You ask the stone for help with a task. It speaks a few motivating words related to the task at hand, which grants you a +1 item bonus to the first skill check you attempt within 1 minute. You become temporarily immune to the effects of all _stones of encouragement_, even ones other than the one you activated, for 1 day. You can still hear the encouraging words of different stones if you hold them, but they don't provide any benefits.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />

<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 165

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You traded your senses to a [hag](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=59) for unrivaled expertise stolen from various souls who were once the greatest in their field. Your _bargained contract_ is sealed by sleeping with a pitch-black stone under your pillow every night. Choose one skill when you seal this _bargained contract_. You become an expert in that skill; if you were already an expert, you become a master, and if you were already a master, you become legendary. Once per day, from any distance, the hag that holds your contract can take over your senses for 10 minutes, during which time the hag hears, sees, smells, tastes, and feels everything you would typically experience. During this time, you are [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) by your own disjointed senses.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You place the stone sealing your bargained contract in your mouth. For the next 10 minutes, you gain a +3 status bonus to skill checks using the skill you chose for your contract.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 92

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Also known as a loadstone, this small stone appears nonmagical and has a lovely sheen, giving the impression that it could be a valuable or a notable item or a magic stone of some kind. When you’ve carried the stone on your person for 1 minute, its curse activates: the stone’s size does not change, but it suddenly increases in weight to 5 Bulk. This additional weight does not cause the stone to deal more damage if thrown or used as a weapon. It reappears in your possessions within 1 minute if you discard it, and can’t be destroyed or thrown away permanently, or even placed in a container that would reduce or negate its Bulk (like a [_bag of holding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249)), until it is subject to a [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250) spell or similar magic effect. Once the curse has activated for the first time, the stone fuses to you.

</column>

May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse **Source** [Pathfinder #154: Siege of the Dinosaurs](/Sources.aspx?ID=31) pg. 76 **Price** 1,200 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Base Weapon** [Javelin](/Weapons.aspx?ID=71) --- This stone-headed _+2 striking [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) [javelin](/Weapons.aspx?ID=71)_ draws forth the power of the earth itself to strike at enemies. **Activate** Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You hurl the _stoneraiser javelin_ at an unoccupied space within 30 feet. The javelin’s power flows into the ground, which erupts in a 5-foot-radius burst of razor-sharp stalagmites. The stalagmites are 10 feet tall. Everything on each side of the stalagmites has cover from creatures on the opposite side, and the stalagmites’ spaces are difficult terrain. A creature takes 4d4 piercing damage for every move action it takes that enters at least one of the affected spaces. Each 5-foot-by-5-foot section has AC 10, Hardness 14, and 30 Hit Points. It’s immune to critical hits and precision damage. A destroyed section can be moved through freely. The stalagmites crumble to dust after 1 minute. Any creature in the area when the stalagmites appear is pushed to the nearest unoccupied space of its choice; this movement is [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=451). Pushed creatures must attempt a DC 28 Reflex saving throw or take 4d4 piercing damage. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

Your skin becomes a canvas that records history as you learn it. When you receive the tattoo, choose a [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill. You can add the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait to the [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) action in order to study your tattoos, granting you a +1 item bonus to your check using the chosen Lore skill. A storied skin tattoo starts with an icon that represents a central event in your subject of study and is usually placed on the forehead or over the heart. Each time you learn about a major event in the history of that subject, an image, design, or symbol appears on your skin to represent the event.

**Activate—Living History** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The tattoo’s design animates for 1 round, crudely portraying some scene associated with the chosen Lore skill.

**Failure** The foe takes full damage and is buffeted by winds for 1 round, taking a –2 circumstance penalty to ranged attack rolls and a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its fly Speed.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the foe takes double damage.

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

_Storm breaths_ are bottles of temperamental lightning captured during storms on the [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4), releasing small charges of static energy any time they're touched. The first _storm breaths_ were created by [Ranginori's](/Deities.aspx?ID=106) faithful following the Elemental Lord's return from a long imprisonment, but the recipe has since been duplicated across the multiverse. After inhaling _storm breath_, you gain resistance 5 to both electricity and sonic. You can exhale the storm breath as a bolt of lightning, dealing 4d12 electricity damage to all creatures in a 30-foot line, with a DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save.

>
[Storm Chair](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1164)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Electricity" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=56" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 91

**Price** 4,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This traveler's chair uses magic and Stasian technology, storing up power in its Stasian coils to arc lightning through your foes and grant brief spurts of flight.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You create a ball of electricity around the chair, surrounding it in a damaging aura of electricity and using electromagnetism to briefly levitate. For 1 minute, you gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed and adjacent creatures that hit you with a melee attack, as well as creatures that touch or hit you with an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack, take 2d6 electricity damage each time. As normal, this applies to creatures who choose to touch you, not when you touch or attack another creature.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You release the majority of the stored up energy from your _storm chair_, devastating foes in a chain of electricity. This has the effects of [_chain lightning_](/Spells.aspx?ID=33) with a DC of 31.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast a 6th-level [_lightning bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=172) (DC 33).

;  **Effect** You try to divert the electricity off course, to be absorbed by _storm flash_. Choose one eligible creature to protect and roll a melee attack roll against the DC of the electricity effect. If you succeed, the chosen creature takes no electricity damage from the triggering effect.

---

This iridescent, black _[+2](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [shock](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2847) [thundering](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850) [fighting fan](/Weapons.aspx?ID=284)_ is crafted from the crackling feathers of [thunderbirds](/Monsters.aspx?ID=825) to resemble one of the beast’s mighty wings. Channeling the avian’s tempestuous nature, you are surrounded by a stormy shell of wind and electricity while wielding a storm herald, granting you resistance 5 to electricity and sonic damage.

**Activate—Call the Storm** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You channel the full might of a storm with you as its epicenter. All creatures within 30 feet take 3d10 electricity damage and 3d10 sonic damage (DC 30 basic Reflex save).

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include feathers from a [thunderbird](/Monsters.aspx?ID=825).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Stormbreaker Fulu](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5084)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Fulu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=378" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Talisman" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=155" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 221, [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 75

**Price** 1,900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Trigger** You would be forced to move, you would be teleported, or you would take cold, electricity, or sonic damage.</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This unassuming paper tag is inscribed with magical symbols. When you activate the fulu, it vanishes in a wisp of cloud, and you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 15 to [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), and [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) damage until the end of your next turn. For that duration, you [ignore difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) from wind and weather, and you can’t be forcibly moved or teleported unless the effect [counteracts](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) the fulu (DC 40). These protections apply against the triggering effect.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Triumph of the Tusk</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #208: Hoof, Cinder, and Storm](/Sources.aspx?ID=250) pg. 78

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These shards of coalesced necromantic essence are sometimes found in the wake of an ancestor storm. Howling spirits are faintly visible, trapped inside the jagged, dark-green glass.

You can use the shard to cow the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) or briefly release the tormented souls from inside the glass. While you hold the stormshard, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) checks to [influence](/Rules.aspx?ID=1830) the undead. In addition, you can [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) undead creatures, even if those creatures are [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) or otherwise [immune](/Rules.aspx?ID=2313) to [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), or [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects.

**Activate—Free the Spirits** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You briefly release the spirits from the _stormshard_ before drawing them back into the glass. Each creature in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) takes 4d8 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage (DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save). You treat the result of your saving throw as one degree of success better than its outcome.

</column>

</title>

---

This green spellbook with gold trim contains a cautionary story about a boy who was eaten by a [wolf](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=485) after he previously lied about wolf attacks. When opened, the engravings on the front seem to move in a loop, enacting this story. 

**Activate—Hoodwink** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature succeeds, but doesn’t critically succeed, at a Perception check to disbelieve an illusion spell you’ve cast today;  **Effect** You quickly tell a fib to try to smooth over the inconsistencies in your illusion. Attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check against the triggering creature’s [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2040) DC. If you succeed, the creature doesn’t disbelieve the [illusion](/Rules.aspx?ID=267).

    level="1"
    right="Item 7"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Strand of the Seven Births](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4007)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 81

**Price** 300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This strand of charms depicts the legendary [harpy](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3046) Ekriathe and her six reincarnated successors. Each charm can be removed and activated. When all of the charms are consumed, the strand becomes inert.

**Activate—Hero-God's Whisper** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297), [light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640))    **Effect** You detach a charm, which creates a glowing ghostly image of the hero-god depicted on it. This image sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 20-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet) for 1 hour. Allies within the image’s bright light hear the constant whispers of Ekriathe or her successor’s voice, and they gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws against [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) effects. Enemies entering or ending their term in the image’s radius of bright light must attempt a DC 23 Will save. On a failure, the target is [fascinated](/Conditions.aspx?ID=72) and takes a –2 status penalty to auditory-based [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=3303) checks while they remain in the radius. Creatures that succeed against this effect are temporarily immune for the next 24 hours.

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 581

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

A _striking_ rune stores destructive magic in the weapon, increasing the weapon damage dice it deals to two instead of one. For instance, a _+1 striking dagger_ would deal 2d4 damage instead of 1d4 damage.

 You can upgrade the _striking_ rune already etched on a weapon to a stronger version, increasing the values of the existing rune to those of the new rune. You must have the formula of the stronger rune to do so, and the Price of the upgrade is the difference between the two runes’ Prices.

[Stumbling Fulu](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2043)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Fulu" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=378" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 79

**Price** 10 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Duration** 1 hour

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The [kitsune](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=38) who first created a _stumbling fulu_ advised the user to tuck the fulu under the target's belt for maximum effect. When the creature to which the fulu is affixed completes a Stride action, the creature must attempt a DC 17 Reflex save. On a failure, some element of the armor the fulu is affixed to comes undone, making the wearer [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3). On a critical failure, the target falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and is clumsy 2. Stupor poison is a more potent distillation of [lethargy poison](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3340). Further exposure to stupor poison doesn’t require the target to attempt additional saving throws; only failing a saving throw against an ongoing exposure can progress its stage.

This thick piece of leather decorated with purple threads makes an attractive necktie but also serves a functional purpose: protecting the neck from hits that you don’t see coming. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against attacks while [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) from [flanking](/Rules.aspx?ID=2375).

**Activate—Stretch out Stock** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _sturdy neck_ stock expands to cover not only your neck but also your shoulders and the back of your head. For 1 minute, you aren’t off-guard to [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79), [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=96), or flanking creatures, or creatures using [surprise attack](/Feats.aspx?ID=6259) of your level or lower.

For 1 minute, you aren’t off-guard to hidden, undetected, or flanking creatures, or creatures using surprise attack of your level or lower.
